name: NJ-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Josh Gottheimer running with a massive cash advantage ($12.8M vs ~$8K)
Prediction markets price Gottheimer at 95-97% to win
District leans Democratic (PVI D+2) with a favorable environment for incumbents
Republican challenger is minimally funded with no polling presence
model.rationale: The baseline model (D+17.9) and prediction markets (95-97% Democratic) align with overwhelming incumbent advantages in fundraising and a D+2 district. I shade slightly toward the markets given the challenger's near-total lack of resources.
model.watch: A late surge in national Republican spending or a major scandal involving Gottheimer could tighten the race, though the funding gap makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 5th District leans slightly Democratic, and incumbent Josh Gottheimer is seeking another term with every structural advantage. He has raised over $4.7 million this cycle and holds nearly $12.8 million on hand, while Republican Sean Kirrane has raised under $60,000 with almost nothing banked. No independent groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

There are no public general-election polls, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Gottheimer's chances at 95 to 97 percent, consistent with the quantitative baseline of a roughly 18-point Democratic margin. With no expert ratings and no polling, uncertainty remains somewhat elevated, but the combination of incumbency, money, and district lean points clearly to a Safe Democratic hold.
